title: This Glass Drop Stops a Bullet, but a Pinch Destroys It

scenes.text: A glass drop that stops a bullet, but dies from a pinch.
Drip molten glass into cold water. You get a glass tadpole with a thin tail, called a Prince Rupert's drop.
Hammer the head. Nothing. Shoot it, and the bullet shatters instead.
Snap the tail, and cracks race to the head at over 4,000 miles an hour. It turns to powder.
The outside cooled first and clamps the inside at 50 tons per square inch. The tail is the leak.
Scientists puzzled over it for 400 years. A bullet can't. A pinch can.

description:
A glass drop that can stop a bullet, but shatters to powder if you pinch its tail.
Prince Rupert's drops are made by dripping molten glass into cold water. The surface cools first and clamps the head under about 50 tons per square inch of compression, so hammers and even bullets fail; snap the thin tail and cracks race through it at over 4,000 miles per hour. Purdue researchers mapped the stresses in 2017, 400 years after the drops first baffled scientists.
What would you test it against first?
first_comment: Bonus: Prince Rupert gave five of these to King Charles the Second in 1661, and the court used them as party tricks. What would you test one against?
